Specialty and niche lenders.name: Specialty, niche and digital lenders
Specialty and niche lenders.description: These banks and bank-owned lenders build national lending lines in narrow areas such as mortgage warehouse funding, association banking, auto finance, leasing and digital banking. They earn loan spread on concentrated books, with margins tied to the cycle in the niche and to less sticky wholesale or online funding.

Super-regional universal banks.name: Large national banks and small community banks
Super-regional universal banks.description: These bank holding companies take deposits and lend to households and businesses, ranging from the largest US money-center banks to small local community banks. They earn mostly net interest spread, plus fees from payments, wealth and capital markets. The layer is mixed by size, so scale and funding costs differ widely within it.

Deposit-funded retail and commercial ban.name: Deposit-funded regional retail and commercial banks
Deposit-funded retail and commercial ban.description: These regional bank and thrift holding companies gather deposits through branches and lend to households and local businesses. Spread income is the main earner, with some trust, insurance and mortgage fees.

extra.name: Global and foreign universal banks
extra.description: Large international and non-US banking groups with retail, corporate and investment banking across many countries. They earn net interest income plus trading, advisory and wealth fees, and are set apart by home-market scale and foreign regulation.

extra.name: Custody and asset servicing banks
extra.description: Banks that mainly provide custody, fund administration and investment servicing to institutional investors. They earn mostly servicing and management fees rather than loan spread.

Global and foreign universal banks.name: Foreign banking groups earning loan interest
Global and foreign universal banks.description: Large non-US banking groups, mostly Canadian, Japanese, Spanish, British and Indian, that make loans to retail and corporate customers across many countries. They earn mainly from interest on loans, with a smaller share from fees on managed money, and are set apart by foreign home markets and regulation.

Custody and asset servicing banks.name: Custody, servicing and wealth fee banks
Custody and asset servicing banks.description: Banks that hold assets, administer funds and manage money for institutional and wealthy clients. They earn mainly from servicing and management fees, with loan interest as a secondary source, which sets them apart from loan-driven banks.
